core_obligations: Pencil step (proof lines 2928-2936): two independent sections s, t give the pencil map with f = s/t; if it is not generically etale then f lies in k(X^{(p)}) by the unwind proposition.

All-quotients step (proof lines 2937-2950): with a basis s_0, ..., s_r and f_i = s_i/s_0, if every f_i lies in k(X^{(p)}) then the map given by the generated invertible subsheaf L' factors through X^{(p)}, the extension over the affine chart to the whole smooth curve being supplied by the normal-curve lemma.

Factorization and degree (proof lines 2950-2962): writing X -> X^{(p)} -> P^r for the factorization, N = psi^*O(1) pulls back to L' along the Frobenius with independent coordinate sections, and d = deg(L) >= deg(L') = deg(F) deg(N) = p deg(N), giving possibility (2) with d' <= d/p.
proof_roadmap: Form the pencil map from two independent sections and test generic etaleness.
If the pencil fails, test all coordinate quotients against k(X^{(p)}) and factor the full map through the Frobenius twist.
Extend the factored map over the normal curve and pull back O(1) to obtain N on X^{(p)}.
Compare degrees through the relative Frobenius to conclude d' <= d/p.
difficulty_reason: The lemma dichotomizes any linear system in characteristic p (statement lines 2915-2926): either a generically etale pencil exists, or the Frobenius twist X^{(p)} carries a system of degree at most d/p. The proof (lines 2928-2962) runs: pencil test via the unwind proposition, the all-quotients factorization through X^{(p)} with extension over the normal curve, pullback of O(1), and the degree identity deg(L') = p deg(N). Every step is present with no omissions. H3: the Frobenius factorization mechanism is genuine characteristic-p geometry.
